panel.introduction: Methone is a tiny, egg-shaped moon between Mimas and Enceladus. Cassini found an exceptionally smooth surface with a darker oval on its leading side.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: Cassini’s 2012 clear-filter image at about 27 m/pixel, projected onto the measured ellipsoid. Approximate illumination correction preserves the darker leading-side oval; gray grid marks unavailable coverage. Methone is exceptionally smooth at this resolution. Tiny isolated source-image spots may be detector artifacts.
controls.title: ISS clear-filter image
controls.summary: The darker oval is visible at about 27 m per source pixel. Gaps are marked; tiny isolated spots may be detector noise.

charts.alt: Cassini VIMS · 2012-05-20 · about 58° phase angle. Mean disk-integrated spectrum from five cubes, re-normalized by Hedman et al. (2024) to a dimensionless brightness coefficient. Bars show the released 1σ statistical errors. Three channel gaps follow the author notebook; omitted rows remain in the CSV. This model-normalized coefficient is not absolute albedo or a spatial composition map.
